text:
2 October 2026
Today in History

1652
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
The weather is not discussed for the day.
Pieter Brackenier was again subjected to cross-examination that day.
He was found guilty and sentenced to 100 lashes, while being tied to the mast of a ship. He was also to be kept aboard the ship as a “prisoner” for a period of time.
A decision was also taken that day to establish (steam) kettles some distance from the fort, near the Salt River.
Because of the distance from the fort, it was believed that the smell and smoke would not disturb anyone.
The idea was that whales would be slaughtered there and that the oil could be extracted using the kettles.
The kettle sites could also serve as observation points for whales.
Towards evening, the men who had sailed to Hout Bay returned.
They brought back reports of the most beautiful indigenous forests imaginable.
They also found a strong-flowing river with clear, clean water that tasted fresh and good.
The bay would also provide excellent protection against the Cape's winds and storms.
Harry also reported that a British ship had, on one occasion, given him two bags of rice there.

1653
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Several Saldanhars arrived at the fort during the morning.
They reported that the rest of their community was on its way, together with their livestock and worldly possessions.
Some of them offered ostrich eggs as a medium of exchange.
During the afternoon a severe and powerful wind began to blow.

1654
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Daybreak brought a stormy and cloudy day to the Cape.
The wind blew constantly and strongly from the south-south-east.
Shortly after daybreak, news was received that the wheat, barley and other grain crops had literally been flattened and blown down onto the ground.
Later during the day, news was received that exactly the same thing had happened to the crops on Robben Island.
The remainder of the gardens, covering approximately six morgen of land, remained undamaged.
The gardens contained, among other things, cabbage, beetroot, carrots, turnips and many kinds of herbs.
Reading between the lines, it is clear that Commander van Riebeeck was very proud of what had been achieved at the Cape.

Saturday, 2 October 1655
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Daybreak brought a cool, cloudy day to the Cape, with little wind to speak of.
All available personnel were sent to the forests that day, where the woodcutters felled beams and sawed planks.
The beams and planks were dragged and carried to the “road.”

1656
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Daybreak at the Cape is described as dark and misty.
The wind blew from the north-west and is described as little more than a breeze.

1657
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Daybreak is described as dark and cloudy, accompanied by severe gusts of wind and rain.
Late in the afternoon it began to hail.
The hailstones are described as being as large as pigeon eggs, with some as large as tennis balls.

1658
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
The weather for the day is described as pleasant and warm.
The sheep thieves were publicly punished that day.
Three cattle, a calf and twelve sheep were exchanged with the indigenous people.
News was also received that some serious disease had broken out among the indigenous people. Doman was sent to establish whether the rumours concerning the disease were true.
An important Resolution was also adopted that day.
In the past, Free Burghers and personnel from the fort had indiscriminately felled trees, both large and small.
Timber was sold to ships and sometimes simply cut down to clear land for cultivation.
This practice was stopped that day.
Trees on allocated private property could be used for private purposes. Trees and timber not on private property had to be purchased from the Company at 10 stuivers per load.
Anyone found guilty of abusing the timber regulations would be fined three rixdollars.
No one was permitted to cut timber belonging to the Company's fence or adjoining the gardens.

1659
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Daybreak is described as cloudy, with rain from time to time.
As on the previous day, the wind continued to blow from the north-west.

1835
The recollections of J.H. Hatting during the Great Trek

1839
Panda pointed out to the Volksraad that Tambuza, together with a man named Noudhlela, had been one of the principal leaders on the night of the Bloukrans massacres.
According to him, the tactic of first sending gifts and then wanting to make peace was an old tactic of Dingaan's.
He pointed out to the Volksraad that the Zulu monarchy was still in place, and that the Zulu people were as numerous as the grass of the veld.
Panda concluded his argument by saying that it was only a matter of time before Dingaan took action.
The Volksraad subsequently decided to hold Tambuza temporarily as a prisoner of war.

Monday, 2 October 1836
From the diary of Louis Tregardt
Today was a particularly joyful day for the Tregardt family, but also a very sad one.
Louis writes that his wife gave birth to twin baby boys.
The younger of the twins, however, died four hours after birth.
Louis further writes that Mafier, probably a cattle herder, ran away.
Doors shot a rhinoceros that day.
Doors was Theodorus de Buys, a son of Coenraad de Buys.
The De Buys family lived in the Soutpansberg–Blouberg area.

Monday, 2 October 1837
From the diary of Louis Tregardt
As was customary, the Tregardt party had been up and about for a long time by the last crow of the cock.
When they were ready to inspanned, however, yet another of Louis's oxen was missing.
Strijdom thought that the ox had probably wandered off during the night towards the cattle and was most likely with the herd.
Louis left the matter there, made his plans and trekked on without the ox.
As a precaution, however, he sent some of his herdsmen back along the spoor to search for it.
Although the herdsmen later returned empty-handed, they had at least brought back a sheep that had fallen into a pitfall.
The party trekked as far as the Baloela River that day.
On the way, another two cattle fell into pit traps.
Carolus lost a fine verse that day.
According to Punt, in Tregardt se laaste skof, they outspanned at what later became the farm Adriaansdraai.

Monday, 2 October 1837
From the diary of Reverend Erasmus Smit
The party only got underway at approximately eight o'clock that morning.
Piet Retief, unusually, was part of the party.
During the morning Retief received a letter from B. Liebenberg. The letter had already been sent by messenger on 30 September.
Liebenberg basically informed them that the laager where they had been staying was not far from where that morning's trek began.
According to him, there was more than enough firewood, excellent grazing for the livestock and sufficient water.
The Retief party indeed arrived there at approximately one o'clock in the afternoon and outspanned.
Among those at the laager were the families of B. Liebenberg, W. Bezuidenhout and Coenraad Meyer.
On 6 September, several families had moved ahead with nine kakebeen wagons. According to the reverend, the plan had been to go hunting.
Six of the nine wagons later returned, but three families continued farther ahead.
These were the families of Coenraad Scheepers, Wijnand Mare and Jan Minnaar.
Coenraad Meyer, who was the leader of this group of Voortrekkers, was obviously displeased and considered their action dangerous.
Meyer took action and had the people turn back along their spoor.

Tuesday, 2 October 1838
From the diary of Reverend Erasmus Smit
Reverend Smit writes that he visited those who had travelled to Port Natal.
Towards evening he withdrew to “his private” place of prayer outside the laager and prayed to his Creator.

1857
The birth of Marthinus Theunis Steyn
The birth of Marthinus Theunis Steyn, who would become the last President of the Orange Free State, took place on this day.
President Steyn was born on the farm Rietfontein, just outside Winburg.
During his life he was, among other things, a solicitor, advocate, judge and ultimately the last State President of the Orange Free State.
The Bloemfontein Conference of 31 May 1899 was his final attempt to prevent the Anglo-Boer War from becoming a reality.
During the war he spent much of his time in the field with General Christiaan de Wet.
He was part of General de Wet's force that invaded the Cape Colony in February 1901.
On one occasion near Reitz in the Free State, he was nearly captured.
He escaped thanks to his brave rear rider, Ruiter, who acted calmly but quickly.
After the Peace of Vereeniging in July 1902, he left South Africa to receive medical treatment, including treatment for his eyes.
In 1905 he returned to his beloved Free State together with his wife.
This great national figure died in Bloemfontein on 28 November 1916.

Tuesday, 2 October 1900
Anglo-Boer War
Day 357 of the war
General Redvers Buller arrived at Nylstroom. He captured 600 cattle, 4,000 sheep and 150 ox-wagons loaded with supplies.(One can hardly imagine the sight of so many ox-wagons.)
Colonel Rochfort attacked a commando laager between Johannesburg and Pretoria. Nine burghers were captured.
A Steinaecker's Horse patrol ambushed the laager of General Coetzee near the Sabie.General Coetzee escaped, but left a wagon containing ammunition and rifles behind.Later that evening, a man named S. Smart was attacked and badly mauled by a lion.He was taken to Komatipoort, where he died of his wounds on 4 October 1900.

Wednesday, 2 October 1901
Anglo-Boer War
Day 722 of the war
General J.C. Smuts crossed the railway line between Port Elizabeth and Graaff-Reinet.Three men from General Smuts's commando in the Cape Colony were captured at Kuikendiefontein.
Lord Methuen left Mafeking with a force of 3,000 men and 20 guns. They moved in the direction of Zeerust.
Lord Kitchener decided to place all the so-called “Joiners” and “Hensoppers” together as a single unit, the later so-called “National Scouts,” and make them part of the army.

1901
Anglo-Boer War
Pieter (Piet) Schuil, aged 23, was executed by firing squad in the Rustenburg district on this day.
Piet was a qualified teacher who taught at a school in Rustenburg.
When the war broke out, he joined the commandos in order to do his part.
On 30 September 1901, General Kemp attacked the force of Colonel Kekewich.
The attack took place near Rustenburg on the Selons River.
Colonel Kekewich nevertheless repulsed the attack.
Piet and two other burghers were searching for wounded men near the British positions when they were unexpectedly fired upon.
Piet tore the white flag from his rifle and returned fire.
His companions fled, but Piet was captured and charged with having fought under a white flag.
For this reason he was sentenced to death.
Piet was tied to a chair on the banks of the Selons River and executed by firing squad.
It is recorded that he read from his Bible during the event and refused the brandy that was offered to him.

1910
Hymne Wiess was born on this day.
She is remembered as a lecturer, writer and translator of several works.

1925
The Afrikaans daily newspaper Die Volksblad appeared for the first time on this day.
The newspaper's history can be traced back to 18 November 1904, when the weekly newspaper Het Westen first appeared in Potchefstroom.
From this came Het Volksblad on 26 March 1901, followed by Die Volksblad, which appeared on this day.

1934
2–5 October 1934
The Volkskongres concerning the “Poor White” question began.
This congress was a consequence of the Carnegie Report of 1932.
Leadership was provided by the Dutch Reformed Church.
The initiative eventually resulted in the establishment of the Department of Social Welfare on 1 October 1937.

1947
Susanna Barbara Broers died.
She is remembered as a founding member of the Bond van Afrikaanse Moeders and for establishing several maternity facilities, particularly in rural areas.

1954
A statue of Maria van Riebeeck, wife of Jan van Riebeeck, was unveiled on this day.
The sculptor was Dirk Wolbers, and the statue was cast in Paris.
Maria holds a small bunch of flowers in one hand and a basket of vegetables in the other.

1958
The FAK discussed the possibility of establishing Afrikaans language festivals.

1986
The United States of America imposed sanctions against South Africa.

Why crow in Pitrapaksha, and not any other bird?

1. The Veda already has birds tied to death, but they are warded off, not fed. In Rigveda 10.165 the pigeon is treated as a messenger of Nirriti and Yama, and the owl's shriek is an ill omen.

2. The Ramayana gives the reason for the crow. In the Uttara Kanda, Ravana arrives at King Marutta's yajna and the gods flee in bird forms. Indra becomes a peacock, Varuna a swan, Yama a crow.

3. Pleased with crows, Yama gives them the right to eat the rice offered to the pitrs.

4. So the crow is not a random choice. It is the form Yama himself wore.

5. The feeding is also an old householder duty. Manu 3.92 and Vasistha Dharmasutra 11 list crows among those to be fed on the ground.

6. So the offering is not worship of the crow. It is food given to the creature that Yama's boon connects to the pitrs.

Never gonna happen. Luhnow was fired in January 2020 and suspended for the 2020 season over the sign-stealing scheme. That suspension has long since expired. He is not banned.
His most direct comments came on the Crush City Territory podcast on July 11, 2025, reported by Chandler Rome of The Athletic. He said two or three MLB owners had contacted him about a GM job or a broader sporting-operations role. He turned all of them down. His words: “I don’t think I’m blackballed from baseball like some people think. I know I would do a good job. I know that for a fact. But the reality is I’ve moved on. I’m very happy.” He was raising money for Blue Crow Sports Group, the soccer company he founded in 2021, which owns clubs in Spain, the Czech Republic, the UAE, Cancún, and France.
The line that gets misread — “If the organization ever felt like inviting me, I’d be more than happy to” — was about attending a game at Daikin Park, not taking the job. He said he has not been to an MLB game or the ballpark since he was fired.
Houston is the worst fit of any opening. Crane is the owner who fired him. Bringing him back would reopen the 2017 scandal in the market that lived through it. Crane has also shown he wants a shorter leash than Luhnow had: one-year offers to James Click, an in-season parting with Brown, and Bagwell in the room. Luhnow’s model was the opposite. text:
💜 October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month 💜

Abuse does not always leave bruises where others can see them.

Sometimes it looks like fear. Control. Isolation. Threats. Manipulation. Walking on eggshells.
Sometimes it is being slowly convinced that everything is your fault.
Sometimes it is losing pieces of yourself while trying to keep the peace.

If any of this feels familiar, please hear this clearly:

You are not alone.
You are allowed to ask for help.
You are allowed to tell someone what is happening.
You are allowed to choose safety.

You do not have to have everything figured out before you reach out. Sometimes the first brave step is simply telling one safe person the truth.

If someone you love may be experiencing abuse, listen without judgment. Believe them. Do not shame them for staying or demand to know why they have not left. Leaving can be complicated and dangerous. Help them find safe, informed support.

And as Christians, we must be careful never to use Scripture to pressure someone into remaining where they are being harmed. Faithfulness to God does not require silently enduring abuse.

“The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.”
Psalm 34:18 KJV

💜 NEED HELP?
National Domestic Violence Hotline
📞 Call 1-800-799-SAFE (7233)
💬 Text START to 88788
🌐 Live chat is available through https://t.co/UsC4Ri822a

If you are in immediate danger or a life-threatening situation, call 911.

The National Domestic Violence Hotline provides advocates who can offer support, crisis intervention, safety-planning information and connections to local resources. 

In North Carolina, local domestic-violence agencies serve all 100 counties and may provide crisis lines, emergency shelter, counseling and other survivor services. 

This October, may we pray for those living in fear, support those finding the courage to reach for help, honor survivors rebuilding their lives, and refuse to look away when someone is hurting.

There is hope. There is help. You do not have to walk through this alone. 💜🙏🏻

text:
October 1; October 14; October 28 The Feast of the Holy Protection of the Theotokos (Virgin Mary's Cerement; Protecting Veil of the Theotokos; Intercession of the Theotokos; Agia Skepi; Pokrov of the Most Holy Theotokos)
.
"From time immemorial, the Church has celebrated the Most-holy Theotokos as the Patroness and Protectress of the Christian people, who, by her intercessory prayers, implores God's mercy for us sinners. The help of the Most-holy Mother of God has been clearly shown numerous times, to individuals and to nations, in peace and in war, in monastic deserts and in densely populated cities. The event that the Church commemorates and celebrates today confirms the Theotokos' consistent protection of Christian people. On October 1, 911, during the reign of Emperor Leo the Wise, there was an All-night Vigil in the Blachernae Church of the Mother of God in Constantinople. The church was full of people. St. Andrew the Fool-for-Christ was standing in the rear of the church with his disciple Epiphanius.
.
At four o'clock in the morning, the Most-holy Theotokos appeared above the people, holding her omophorion outstretched as a protective covering for the faithful. She was clothed in gold-encrusted purple, and shone with an ineffable radiance, surrounded by apostles, saints, martyrs and virgins. St. Andrew said to Blessed Epiphanius: ``Do you see, brother, the Queen and Lady of all praying for the whole world?'' Epiphanius replied: ``I see, Father, and am struck with amazement!'' The Feast of the Protection was instituted to commemorate this event, and to remind us that we can prayerfully receive the unceasing protection of the Most-holy Theotokos in any time of difficulty."
.
Some additional information about this feast and the Russian Church:
.
"In the PROLOGUE, a Russian book of the twelfth century, a description of the establishment of the special Feast marking this event states, "For when we heard, we realized how wondrous and merciful was the vision... and it transpired that Your holy Protection should not remain without festal celebration, O Ever-Blessed One!"
Therefore, in the festal celebration of the Protection of the Mother of God, the Russian Church sings, "With the choirs of the Angels, O Sovereign Lady, with the venerable and glorious prophets, with the First-Ranked Apostles and with the Hieromartyrs and Hierarchs, pray for us sinners, glorifying the Feast of your Protection in the Russian Land." Moreover, it would seem that St Andrew, contemplating the miraculous vision was a Slav, was taken captive, and became the slave of the local inhabitant of Constantinople named Theognostus.
.
Churches in honor of the Protection of the Mother of God began to appear in Russia in the twelfth century. Widely known for its architectural merit is the temple of the Protection at Nerl, which was built in the year 1165 by holy Prince Andrew Bogoliubsky. The efforts of this holy prince also established in the Russian Church the Feast of the Protection of the Mother of God, about the year 1164.
.
At Novgorod in the twelfth century there was a monastery of the Protection of the Most Holy Theotokos (the so-called Zverin monastery) In Moscow also under Tsar Ivan the Terrible the cathedral of the Protection of the Mother of God was built at the church of the Holy Trinity (known as the church of St Basil the Blessed).
.
On the Feast of the Protection of the Most Holy Theotokos we implore the defense and assistance of the Queen of Heaven, "Remember us in your prayers, O Lady Virgin Mother of God, that we not perish by the increase of our sins. Protect us from every evil and from grievous woes, for in you do we hope, and venerating the Feast of your Protection, we magnify you."
Note: the Church of Greece has moved the celebration of Agia Skepi to the 28th of October in commemoration of the great help and protection of the Theotokos to the Greek nation throughout its history, and especially during World War II:
.
"The role of faith in Virgin Mary in Epirus is also outstanding during the Second World War. Her role was catalytic not only because she constituted the basis of people’s faith, but also because, with her miraculous interventions, she proved to have been the greatest ally of the Greek army on the snowy and rough mountains of Epirus.
.
Of course, miracles and apparitions were reported in many regions of Greece during the war, but at the front, at the Greek – Albanian borders and on Pindus, Virgin Mary was the protector and the leader of those who fought for their country under difficult circumstances. Their faith was so strong that they could see her encouraging them and “covering” them protectively, while they were fighting on the snowy mountains of Pindus and Albania.
.
The account given by Vassililki Bouri, niece of Spyridon Houliaras, who fought at the borders, is characteristic. According to it, Spyridon Houliaras used to narrate incidents of the war to his relatives before he died. The one that affected him the most, however, was a miracle of Virgin Mary. While the soldiers were fighting under really adverse conditions, Virgin Mary appeared in front of them and as a protector “covered” them with her mantle and led them towards their enemy, ready to confront them.
.
This miracle is also corroborated by the accounts of other soldiers of that time who fought on the mountains of Pindus. At the front, Greek soldiers saw the same vision everywhere: at nights, they could see a tall, slim woman figure walking with her kerchief resting on her shoulders. For the soldiers she was no other than Virgin Mary, the defender general of Greeks.
.
Tasos Rigopoulos, a soldier in 1940, reports from the front: I’m writing from an eagle’s nest 400 metres higher than the top of Parnitha. Everything around me is snowwhite. The reason I’m writing […] is to share with you what I’ve experienced, what I saw with my own eyes; something that I’m afraid you won’t believe if you hear it from others. A few moments before dashing against the blockhouses of Morova we saw a tall woman dressed in black standing still some 13 metres away. The guard yelled: “Identify yourself”. There was no answer. He yelled angrily once more. At that moment, as if struck by electricity, we all whispered: “Panaghia!”. She hurled herself at the enemy as if she had eagle wings. We followed her. We could constantly sense the bravery she was transmitting to us. We fought hard for a whole week until we finally took the Ivan-Morova blockhouses. […] She was always dashing forth. And when, victorious at last, we were advancing to defenseless Koritsa, our Defender turned into steam, smooth smoke, and vanished into thin air”.  On the mountain ridge of Ronteni, the soldiers of the 51st independent battalion, under the commands of major Petrakis also witnessed a miracle. From the 22nd of January and on, every evening at half past nine the enemy’s heavy artillery commenced fire against the battalion and the road that was used by transport vehicles. There was a lot of nervousness and heavy casualties. The daring scouts were unable to locate the enemy’s artillery. Apparently, the enemy was changing its position every evening. The situation was really desperate. It was an evening in February when the enemy artillery was heard firing once again. “Panaghia, help us, save us”, shouted the major spontaneously. Suddenly, a bright cloud came into sight from a distance, something like a halo was formed and the image of Virgin Mary appeared. She started bending towards the ground and stopped right over a ravine. Everybody in the battalion shivered as they witnessed the miracle. “Miracle!”, they shouted and they prayed. Immediately, they sent a message to the Greek artillery, the Greek canons fired, and right after that there was a silence. The Greek bombs had achieved a perfect strike.
.
“No matter how faith is expressed during war, it is certain that it offers assistance to the soldier who is tested. And the image of the protector makes him hopeful and optimistic. …People from Arta, fighting at the front, were afraid neither of mortars nor of enemy bullets, as long as they had the image of Panaghia in front of them…”.  Yiannis Tsarouchis, after having painted “The Virgin of Victory” on the cap of a box of herring, having in mind a badly painted picture of the Virgin that was going around the camp, he was on his way to the commander of the battalion in order to present his work. The painting had already acquired a fame of being miraculous and on his way to the commander some soldiers from Arta “being in a state of religious excitement, demanded that the miraculous icon spend at least one night at their camp. All the soldiers were shouting: “The Virgin, the Virgin. Leave it here for one night”. Suddenly, the alarm sounded. […] we lied down, according to the orders we had. None of the soldiers from Arta did the same. “Hey! Comrade! How can you be scared when you hold the Virgin in your hands?”, one said”.
.
It was also characteristic that on the military identification cards, right next to the personal details there was a picture of Virgin Mary. And just moments before they attacked, they would pray, shout “Panaghia mou!” (my Virgin) three times, and dash forth.
.
The importance of Virgin Mary’s miraculous interventions was acknowledged right after the end of the Second World War. For this reason, the celebration of Agias Skepis, which in 626 A.D., when Her miraculous intervention saved Constantinople from the Avaroi (Turkish-Mongolian Nomads), was officially established to be celebrated on October 1st, was transferred in 1952 on the 28th of October to remind them of her miraculous intervention during the most difficult period for Greek people."

text:
📍 : Apollo Bunder Docks, Bombay
🗓️ : January 1915
🕒 : 6:00 AM

The massive hull of the S.S. Arabia cuts through the morning mist, slowly docking against the pier. Stepping off the gangway is a 46 year old veteran of global civil rights, a man whose legal exploits abroad have already made him a household name. Yet, upon setting foot on his native soil, he makes a calculated operational decision that completely baffles the elite political class: he vows to keep his mouth shut for an entire year to simply listen to the land. He executes this by purposefully avoiding the comfortable carriages of the wealthy, plunging instead into the suffocating, unsanitary 3rd class compartments of the railways. For over 2 years, he crisscrosses thousands of kilometers, sharing sweat and space with ordinary citizens, realizing a fundamental truth: to move the masses, you must first move with the masses.

When he finally stepped into the active arena in 1917, it wasn’t through grand national speeches, but through a high-stakes, cinematic showdown in a remote courtroom that completely shocked the colonial empire. 

Summoned by desperate local farmers to investigate an exploitative indigo farming arrangement, his presence instantly terrified the local administration. Dragged into a packed courtroom for defying an order to leave the district, the magistrate, desperate to de-escalate tension, offered to release him instantly on a ₹100 bail. 

What did this lawyer do? He looked the judge dead in the eye and flatly refused to pay. He calmly stated that he would rather take the prison sentence. 

The courtroom fell into absolute chaos. The colonial legal system had no protocol for a man who actively wanted to go to jail instead of paying a trivial sum. Utterly paralyzed by his defiance and terrified of the gathering crowd outside, the magistrate was forced to release him without any bail whatsoever and eventually dropped the case entirely. It was the first time in modern history that the British Empire was forced to take a public step backward, completely bewildered by a weapon they did not understand. 

Yet, the deepest paradox of his character was just beginning to unfold. Upon his arrival in India, the British Raj had decorated him with the prestigious Kaiser-i-Hind gold medal, the highest civilian honor. He hadn't won it for opposing the crown, but for his fierce loyalty to it, specifically for raising a volunteer medical ambulance corps to assist British soldiers during imperial wars in South Africa. 

Then, in late 1918, this vocal apostle of peace made a bizarre, staggering ideological pivot that left his nationalist allies questioning his sanity. He voluntarily offered his services to the British Viceroy as a literal "Recruiting Sergeant" for the British Indian Army in World War I. Traveling across rural districts in ox-carts, the very man who preached absolute non-violence began aggressively urging young peasants to pick up rifles and fight for the empire in Europe in exchange for future political credit. 

The local activists who had just risked everything alongside him in courtrooms were left utterly disgruntled, blindsided, and deeply disillusioned by this apparent hypocrisy. The rural masses flatly refused to enlist, leaving the entire movement fractured. 

It leaves modern minds with an intoxicating historical puzzle. Was this man a deeply calculating British loyalist playing a generational chess match, a radical independent thinker too unpredictable for his own allies, or the ultimate saintly figure history remembers?

text:
*INDIA WINS FREEDOM: A STORY OF GLORIUS JOINT EFFORT*

If you want to see how India won freedom, don't look at a solo photo. *Look at a group photo.*

*Our freedom is a superhit friendship film.* A Hindu poet wrote a line, *a Muslim friend sang it*, a Sikh brother shouted it, and the whole country marched. We won because *we stood together.*

*1. The 82-Year-Old Poet Who Said Yes To India*

In 1857, *Hindu and Muslim soldiers joined hands* and said, *"Let us make India free."* They chose *Bahadur Shah Zafar* — the 82-year-old poet who loved ghazals and pigeons — and said, *"You are our Emperor of Hindustan."*

With *poet's courage*, he smiled and said yes, because *his love for India was bigger than fear.* In Lucknow, *Begum Hazrat Mahal* led with *grace and bravery*, inspiring all. It was a *beautiful beginning — Muslims leading, everyone joining.*

*2. The Doctor Whose Home Was Everyone's Home*

*Hakim Ajmal Khan of Delhi* was a beloved *Unani doctor who treated rich and poor with the same love.* His house was *India's most welcoming home* — Gandhiji rested there, Nehru discussed there, *Hakim Saheb's kitchen happily fed them all.*

He built *Jamia Millia Islamia* so *Hindus and Muslims could study and laugh together*, and said joyfully, *"If Ayurveda and Unani can heal together in one body, Hindus and Muslims can build together in one country!"* That was *healing with harmony.*

*3. The Scholar Who Loved Unity*

*Maulana Abul Kalam Azad* — *scholar, journalist, orator* — was *Gandhiji's close companion* and became *Congress President at a very young age.* He always smiled and said, *"Hindu-Muslim unity is our heartbeat."* As *India's first Education Minister*, he gifted *IITs, Jamia, Sahitya Akademi* to *all children of India.*

*4. The Poet Who Gave Us Our War Cry*

We love shouting *"Inquilab Zindabad!"* That joyful cry was gifted by *Maulana Hasrat Mohani*, who wrote love songs like *"Chupke Chupke Raat Din"* and freedom songs in the same diary. In 1921 he wrote *"Inquilab Zindabad"* and it became *India's heartbeat.* He said with a smile, *"My India is here. My heart is here."*

*5. The Lawyer Who Stood For A Brother*

When *Bhagat Singh* needed a voice, *Asaf Ali* — Delhi's *most respected barrister* — stood up and *fought bravely.* He said, *"He is my country's son, my brother."* A *Muslim lawyer standing proudly for a Sikh revolutionary* — that is *the India we celebrate.*

*6. The Two Friends Who Became One Name*

*Ram Prasad Bismil* wrote *"Sarfaroshi ki tamanna"* and his best friend *Ashfaqulla Khan sang it with joy.* One Hindu, one Muslim, both full of *laughter and dreams.* When offered freedom to betray Bismil, Ashfaq smiled, *"A friend never leaves a friend."* Today children say one name with love: *"Bismil-Ashfaq" — the symbol of unbreakable friendship.*

*7. The Army Where All Prayers Marched Together*

*Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose* built *Azad Hind Fauj* where *all marched together.* His trusted team — *General Shah Nawaz Khan, Colonel Mehboob Ahmed, Captain Abbas Ali* — marched with Hindu, Sikh, Christian soldiers shouting *"Delhi Chalo!"* The nation then shouted with love, *"Lal Qile se aayi awaaz, Sehgal, Dhillon, Shahnawaz!"*

*THE JOYFUL TRUTH*

*India's freedom is a festival of togetherness.* This is *the family album of India.* On *15th August 1947*, the flag went up because *millions of hands — Hindu, Muslim, Sikh, Christian, Parsi, every Indian — pulled it together, with love, with laughter, with hope.*

*Inquilab Zindabad!*

text:
$70,000 A YEAR — OR $0.

Right now, you can take a program that costs tens of thousands of dollars at Stanford and complete it on your own.

119 lectures.
~95 hours.
7 courses.
6 hands-on projects.
And it’s all free on YouTube.

But the biggest cost here isn't money.

The real cost is spending years thinking that access to top-tier knowledge is off-limits to you just because you don't have the "right" degree.

This article offers something free courses usually lack: not just a list of lectures, but a roadmap.

From linear algebra -> kinematics -> computer vision -> control -> reinforcement learning -> to building your own robot.

And most importantly - you aren't just being asked to watch 95 hours of video.

You're being asked to build something.

Now, that’s interesting.

Because six months down the line, the difference between "I watched a Stanford course" and "here’s my robot, here’s the GitHub repo, and here are the performance metrics" could be massive.

I’d recommend saving this article - even if you have absolutely no idea where to start in robotics yet.

text:
In context, David prayed regarding all the materials he and the people provided to build Solomon's temple. Though they had consecrated these things to God, David recognized they all came from God to begin with. Nothing has changed in that regard. We could take the words of this verse and apply them to everything we have, as well as everything we offer.

Further up in the passage, David asks this, "Who then will offer willingly, consecrating himself today to the LORD?" in v.5.

These passages remind us that all things belong to God, and those things we offer willingly are merely giving back to Him that which is already His. 

But David ties one more thing to giving freely back to God—uprightness. Any hypocrite can give to God willingly to be a part of the crowd, a movement, or to be admired in the eyes of many. But God sees the heart. "Uprightness" assumes righteousness, joy, cheerfulness, thanksgiving, and praise. There is no begrudging here, no bitterness, no regret. Just a purity, a holiness of heart only God can see.

If God has pleasure in uprightness, and if my heart is upright as I freely offer these things that already belong to Him, then God shall find pleasure in me. He'll know I'm not greedy or holding anything back from Him, but that I offer it up with thanksgiving and a cheerful heart. 

Even things that aren't material things come from Him, such as...wisdom. Knowledge. The ability to write. Any gift of the Spirit. When we walk in our gifting, we are cheerfully giving back to the LORD as well. These things I offer to God day after day all come from God in the first place. I might not be able to always profess an upright heart, but I can say I give of these things willingly. 

And when we do so, we consecrate ourselves to the LORD. We set ourselves aside for Him. Make ourselves holy for Him.

"All this abundance...comes from Your hand."

All of it. From Him, through Him, and to Him are all things (Romans 11:36). Do you ever just sit back in awe of Him? I moved into my apartment two years ago with very little furniture, my clothing, a couple bookshelves, and some books, and now when I look around, I am astounded every single day by the abundance He has given from His hand.

I have to pause here and brag for a moment... Yesterday, the maintenance guy came to put in a GFCI outlet and as he was leaving, he looked around my living room and said in an appreciative tone, "You have a beautiful home."

I thanked him, and once he had left, I thanked God. If that man only knew the road I had to take to get here, he would know how much his casual complement meant to me. It was the admiration in his voice that made me pause to consider his words. What filled me wasn't pride, just a deep thankfulness for all these wonderful gifts God has given me.

The fact that I have a "beautiful home" after having basically nothing but a car is concrete proof of God's goodness and provision in my life. So thank You, God, for all the abundance You've given me, and for all the opportunities I have to offer it back to You freely, joyfully, and hopefully, with an upright heart.

"God gives the desolate a home to dwell in" (Psalm 68:6a RSV).

"Even the sparrow finds a home" (Psalm 84:3a).

When yields stay higher, Washington borrows and refinances maturing debt at higher rates, pushing federal interest costs up over time.

Higher yields also raise borrowing costs across the economy and can PRESSURE stocks and crypto as bonds offer more competitive returns.

Ray Dalio warns that mounting debt burdens could eventually lead policymakers to turn to money printing and policies that suppress interest rates, ERODING the DOLLAR’s purchasing power.

In that scenario, bondholders could be repaid in full, but receive dollars worth less.

The consequences of America’s debt problem may arrive well before the next generation inherits the bill.

text:
🇺🇸 🇮🇷 Three Carriers and the Diplomacy of Deadlines

Washington has stopped hiding the arithmetic. The Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit are heading to the Middle East, bringing roughly 9,000 additional sailors and Marines to the region. They will join two carriers already on station. Trump says renewed strikes against Iran after the midterms remain an option. The military buildup and the threat now operate on the same calendar.

But a calendar cuts both ways. It signals intent to an adversary while imposing constraints on the power issuing the warning. Announce a deadline, and you gain leverage. You also give your opponent time to prepare.

Tehran knows how to read a calendar. Iranian commanders are reportedly drafting plans for a broader response should major US attacks resume. Not a symbolic retaliation for a symbolic blow, but an escalation designed to restore deterrence. The reported target list extends beyond US assets to countries supporting American operations, potentially reaching beyond the Middle East. Allied groups in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq have reportedly been told to stand ready.

That is Tehran’s answer to mounting pressure: deterrence by invoice. Make the potential cost of military action clear before it happens. The markets have already begun paying. Oil prices jumped more than $4 a barrel following news of the deployment.

Yet Tehran is bargaining from a position of weakness it can no longer conceal. Washington says Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September. Its leadership fears a repeat of January’s unrest, while analysts question whether Iran could sustain a blockade. President Pezeshkian says Tehran will not shy away from dialogue, even as last weekend talks yielded little progress. Iran is therefore pursuing two tracks simultaneously: keeping a diplomatic channel open while preparing for escalation.

Washington faces a different problem: the gap between military power and political purpose. Trump says that most of Iran’s leaders are gone and that Washington does not know whom to deal with. It is a striking admission from a power assembling such an overwhelming naval presence. A deadline needs someone to receive it. A threat requires someone capable of weighing its consequences. And a deal requires someone with the authority to sign it. Tehran has a plan and a channel. Washington has a fleet but apparently no one to call.

Meanwhile, Iraq offers an indication of where the consequences could first be felt. This week, the US-led coalition ended its mission in the country, and the last American troops left their bases in Erbil. Washington is withdrawing from the ground even as it reinforces its presence at sea. Iran and its allies are celebrating what they regard as a victory. Baghdad, meanwhile, has set June 30, 2027, as the deadline for disarming Iran-backed factions. Tehran’s reported military planning is focused on the coming winter. One clock is counting down to a test of Iraqi sovereignty; the other, to a possible war. The armed factions have every incentive to follow the faster one.

Washington and Tehran are now keeping both a diplomatic door open and a military option loaded. This is not a pause in the conflict. It is a contest over leverage, endurance and, ultimately, who blinks first.

Tehran has until the fleet arrives to decide whether its next move will be negotiation or escalation. But Washington, too, must decide what it expects to achieve when the ships arrive.

text:
1. The iQOO 16 is already on sale in China. India is the hard part. There is no India price or launch date yet. Tipsters say it may skip India this year because of memory and component costs. Earlier IMEI listings pointed to global and India testing, so a launch is still possible. Pricing is the real risk.

2. China pricing starts at CNY 5,999, about ₹86,000 on a straight conversion, for 12GB + 256GB. The 16GB + 512GB model is closer to ₹1.07 lakh. The 1TB model is near ₹1.22 lakh.

3. Hardware is not the problem. It has a 2nm Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, plus iQOO’s Q4 gaming chip. The display is a 6.85-inch 2K Samsung M16 LTPO AMOLED, up to 165Hz. Battery is 8,400mAh, with 100W wired and 40W wireless charging. Cameras are a triple 50MP setup, including a 3x periscope, with IP68 and IP69. That is a clear step up from the iQOO 15 on chip and battery.

4. The problem is what that money buys in India. iQOO’s pitch here was performance per rupee, not brand, cameras, software support, or resale.

5. The iQOO 15 launched in the mid-₹60,000s effective, with a sticker around ₹72,999. After hikes, 12GB + 256GB is closer to ₹86,000. The OnePlus 15 is in the same band after its own jump to ₹77,999 / ₹85,999.

6. At that price you are arguing with Samsung, Google, and a discounted OnePlus on updates and resale. iQOO does not win that argument.

7. A normal China-to-India markup on CNY 5,999 is how you land near ₹90,000–1 lakh. That is where it stops making sense. At ₹1 lakh you are mostly paying for the new chip and the bigger battery, not a camera or software experience that justifies Ultra money.

8. This is the same trap OnePlus is already in: strong hardware, weak reason to pick it over phones people already trust at that price.

9. What I would actually pay: a base 12/256 ceiling of ₹75,000. ₹80,000 only with a real bank or exchange offer. At ₹90,000 or above, and especially at ₹1 lakh, it will be a tough sell

26 data center listings in our October inventory are available now or in Q4.

Three of them are 1 MW or more.

There is power. Almost none of it comes in megawatt blocks.

North America, immediate or Q4 2026:

Under 500 kW: 12 listings
500 to 999 kW: 11 listings
1 MW and up: 3 listings
What to budget, per kW per month, space and power:
Under 100 kW: $225–250
100 to 500 kW: $200–250
1 MW and up: $185–250

The $185 end is build-to-suit, not ready-now space.

No planning band for 500 kW to 1 MW this edition. Two listings on our desk in that range: Denver at 750 kW, $190–225, Q4 2026. Utah at 800 kW, $240, Q4 2026, with 500 kW listed as available now. Both are listed offers, not closed deals.
Those bands overlap on purpose. Bigger does not reliably mean cheaper. At size, the differences are availability, credit and delivery date.
Two things the bands don't tell you.

Listed kW is not always one usable block. A campus total can be split across rooms or phases, and a note saying "immediate" can sit beside an install date two quarters out. Ask which one you're being shown.

Every quarter needs a year. "Out till Q4" means nothing on its own.

At 1 MW and up, plan six to twelve months. Investment-grade credit is the main gate at that size, and some providers want to meet you before committing a full megawatt. Without IGC, a few will start you around 300 kW and consider expansion later. Expansion is not reserved capacity unless it's in writing.

Under 500 kW the picture is different and better. Don't apply megawatt timelines to a single-rack deployment.

October 2026, from 50+ provider responses and our own high-density inventory. Planning ranges, not market averages.

Sizing a deployment? Send the kW, the hardware, the metro and your target date.

text:
A rare Tupinambá Feather Cape, a sacred 17th Century ceremonial cloak crafted by the indigenous Tupinambá people of Brazil....

The cape is crafted from thousands of feathers, primarily from the scarlet ibis (known as guará in Tupi-Guarani language) and incorporates vegetable fibers. These capes were sacred objects used in rituals and held deep cultural and spiritual importance for the Tupinambá people. This particular cape holds immense importance not only for its beauty but also for its exceptional state of preservation. Only a limited number of these capes, around eleven, are known to exist today, with most preserved in European museums. The cape in the image is considered one of the best-preserved examples. 

The Tupinambá, an indigenous people inhabiting the coastal regions of Brazil, were renowned for their sophisticated feather work, creating stunning ceremonial garments, headdresses, and other objects from the vibrant plumage of native birds. These feathered capes were not merely clothing; they were powerful symbols of status, spirituality, and identity, likely worn during important rituals, ceremonies or by tribal leaders. The process of collecting, sorting, and meticulously attaching thousands of individual feathers was an incredibly time-consuming and skilled endeavor, reflecting deep knowledge of ornithology and intricate craftsmanship.

What makes this particular cape at the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium so extraordinary is its condition. It is one of only eleven known Tupinambá feather capes from 16th-17th Centuries AD, that survive globally. Crucially, most of the other ten have suffered significant physical damage over centuries due to their delicate organic nature and the passage of time. The remarkable preservation of this Belgian example offers an unparalleled opportunity to study the artistry, materials, and cultural significance of Tupinambá feather work from a period that saw intense European contact and profound changes for indigenous populations. It stands as a powerful, tangible link to a vibrant indigenous culture that faced immense pressures during the colonial era.

In recent years, there have been efforts to repatriate these culturally significant artifacts to Brazil. For example, a Tupinambá cape held in the National Museum of Denmark for over 300 years was officially returned to Brazil in 2024.

text:
Earth's Ultimate Sanctuaries: Architecture and Survival Beyond the Surface

When evaluating long-term planetary survival and human resilience against catastrophic threats—whether from supervolcano eruptions, coronal mass ejections, abrupt climate shifts, or cosmic impacts—the choice of refuge determines whether human civilization survives or faces extinction. Engineers, planetary scientists, and architects have long debated the viability of different structural environments: subterranean complexes, mountain-interior vaults, high-altitude alpine outposts, underwater habitats, and off-world exoplanet colonies. Each environment presents distinct thermodynamic, structural, and ecological advantages, balanced against severe trade-offs in resource availability, human psychology, and technical complexity. Understanding how these distinct shelter designs function provides a window into the limits of modern structural engineering and closed-loop life support systems.

Subterranean shelters, constructed deep within Earth's crust, exploit the immense mass of soil and bedrock as natural shielding. Located tens to hundreds of meters below the surface, these installations benefit from thermal stability, as Earth's sub-surface temperatures remain relatively constant year-round, significantly reducing the energy required for thermal regulation. Rock and soil layers provide near-complete isolation against atmospheric pollutants, nuclear fallout, surface radiation, and kinetic shockwaves. Modern subterranean construction utilizes deep tunnel boring machines (TBMs) combined with shotcrete reinforcement and active hydraulic drainage systems to counter high lithospheric pressure and groundwater seepage. Furthermore, deep underground installations must incorporate advanced geothermal or nuclear energy systems to power artificial lighting and hydroponic or aeroponic farming, as sunlight is completely absent.

Inside mountain massifs, subterranean shelter engineering reaches a specialized peak. By excavating horizontal adits into stable granite or basalt formations, structural engineers create sanctuaries protected by thousands of meters of solid rock overhead, while retaining horizontal access tunnels that prevent the hydraulic pressure build-up common in deep vertical shafts. The interior geometry of mountain vaults typically features parabolic reinforced concrete arches capable of dispersing tectonic stresses and overpressures from blast waves. These facilities require industrial air filtration complexes equipped with multi-stage high-efficiency particulate air (HEPA) units, activated carbon scrubbers, and positive pressure systems to prevent external gaseous contaminants from entering living quarters. High-altitude mountain-top shelters, positioned above sea level on elevated plateaus, utilize a different survival logic: they escape coastal flooding, storm surges, and dense low-lying toxic atmospheric clouds, relying instead on high-efficiency insulation and wind-resistant aerodynamic domes to withstand severe alpine weather.

Underwater shelters present an entirely different set of environmental challenges, shifting the primary hazard from kinetic impact to immense hydrostatic pressure. Built on continental shelves or anchored to the ocean floor, these submerged habitats rely on high-strength titanium alloys, thick acrylic viewports, and ultra-high-performance concrete engineered to resist hyperbaric stress. The surrounding aquatic environment provides a virtually limitlessly available cooling sink and a source of water that can be desalinated via reverse osmosis and electrolyzed to generate oxygen. However, long-term underwater life support requires precise control over interior gas mixtures—typically continuous oxygen and nitrogen balance—to avoid hyperoxia or decompression sickness, alongside automated scrubbers to eliminate carbon dioxide build-up. The intense mechanical strain caused by corrosion from saltwater and constant hydrodynamic movement makes routine structural monitoring and seal maintenance a continuous operational necessity.

Looking beyond Earth, exoplanet shelters represent the absolute frontier of long-term survival architecture. Located on distant terrestrial worlds within their host stars' habitable zones, these habitats must address extreme variations in gravity, ambient radiation, atmospheric composition, and temperature swings. Because transporting massive construction materials across interstellar distances is physically impractical, off-world shelters rely on automated, in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) using autonomous 3D printers that convert local regolith into radiation-shielding composite shells. These structures are designed as fully closed-loop ecological life support systems (CELSS), where waste products, water, and atmospheric gases are continuously recycled with near-zero loss. Ultimately, while exoplanet colonies offer the ultimate insurance policy against Earth-bound extinction events, their extreme technological distance makes Earth's terrestrial, mountain, and ocean depths the immediate primary strongholds for human continuity.

text:
Space Pirate Sara is the rare adult OVA that treats a galaxy like a debtor’s prison and then has the nerve to give the prisoners the keys, the sword, and the last laugh. Most hentai in the space pirate lane is a costume change. Someone slaps an eyepatch on a body, parks a ship in the background, and runs the same capture loop you have already seen in a dungeon  or a demon castle. Uchuu Kaizoku Sara, released by Pixy across four volumes from spring 2008 to early 2010, refuses that laziness. It is an original video animation in the old sense of the phrase, which is the whole sermon. No broadcast committee sanding the edges. No thirteen episode stretch that dilutes the poison into filler. Four self contained slabs, about twenty seven minutes each, cut from a 2007 Black Lilith visual novel whose own genre label was closer to a threat than a blurb: a no mercy female pirate violation adventure. You are not supposed to come away thinking space is romantic. You are supposed to come away knowing that a title is a leash, that pride is a handle, and that the body which survives the worst room in the empire is the only ballot that counts.

Sara Scorpion is the lesson wearing blonde hair and a mercenary commission. She is an imperial knight who also runs the Scorpion corps, which means the empire already taught her the first rule and she ignored it. A knight is a weapon the throne rents. A pirate is a weapon that invoices the throne. She wants the Sword of Bernstein, the heirloom only Bernstein blood can wake, because the galaxy is a carcass being picked over by rival warlords and the sword is the receipt for the carcass. That quest is the only plot point you need. Everything filthy that follows is the invoice for wanting a clean succession in a dirty empire. She dances through a war ravaged star field the way a legend is supposed to dance, and the OVA immediately shows you the bill. The men who want her do not want her sword arm. Prince Joachim of Blankenheim wants the woman attached to the rumor. Slave routes want the body that the rumor made valuable. The takeaway is ugly and useful. Fame in a collapsing order is not armor. Fame is a catalog entry. You watch her walk into a bargain that looks like piracy and discover it was always a wedding contract written by someone else.

The silver knight beside her is the second lesson, and she is the one who makes the OVA feel like a classic instead of a loop. Sylia, the white silver knight of the Wales lords’ alliance, is pride with a weapon and a reputation. She exists so the story can strip a virtue in public and ask whether the virtue was ever the point. In the usual hentai the proud woman breaks so the viewer can feel the break. Here the break is a curriculum. She is taken, passed among men as a comfort object, and the virginity the ballads were guarding turns out to have been guarding nothing the empire respected. What you are meant to learn is not that purity is fake. It is that purity was always a political costume, issued by the same houses that sell the costume when the ledger demands it. The sex is the lecture. Bodies are pressed to the floor of holds and throne rooms until the idea of an untouched knight sounds like a joke the court told itself. Tentacles do not arrive as a random monster of the week. They arrive as the empire’s unofficial police, a wet bureaucracy that does not bother with trials. Eggs are not a punchline about breeding. They are occupation. Something alive is parked in a body the way a garrison is parked in a city, and the body is expected to carry the garrison and still salute. Against skin, against the soft machinery under the navel, the point is territorial. You do not own the canal you were born with if a stronger flag can moor in it.

That is why the explicit register here feels heavier than the field around it. A lesser space hentai uses tentacles as wallpaper and eggs as a gross out button, then cuts to the next identical moan. Sara lets the act sit long enough to become an argument about property. A c0ck driven into a knight is not just a c0ck. It is a signature on a transfer of title. Cum striped across a uniform is a rewrite of the uniform. The funny part, and it is funny in the mean way only this corner of animation manages, is that the galaxy keeps pretending the paperwork still matters while the paperwork is being used as a rag. You laugh because the dukes still speak in inheritance law while the inheritance is face down and shaking. You stop laughing when you realize the law was only ever the polite version of the same shove.

The third volume is where the OVA stops borrowing from every other captive knight tape and starts owning the shelf. The banquet of the futanari knights is not a kink sticker slapped on at the end. In the anime, unlike some of the game’s wider transformations, the change lands on Sara and Sylia themselves. The women who were inventories become arsenals. What you are supposed to take from that is the nastiest courtesy the story offers. The empire’s favorite trick is to remodel the prisoner into the instrument, then act shocked when the instrument learns the grip. A c0ck grown on a body that spent the previous volumes being opened is not empowerment in the brochure sense. It is stolen hardware. The banquet is a hall where appetite has replaced ceremony, and the two knights are both the feast and, by the end of the logic, the hosts who were late to their own table. Sex between them, and sex that uses them, stops being only violation and becomes fluency. They learn the grammar the men assumed only men could speak. The lesson is not that a new organ fixes a assault . The lesson is that a system which teaches through the body can be answered in the body’s own dialect, and that dialect is obscene on purpose.

Volume four, the reversal of the pirate knight, is why people still call the set a legend instead of a nasty curiosity. Most OVAs in this lane die in the cell. The cell is the product, the escape is a shrug, and the viewer is sent home with the same stain. Sara spends its last stretch refusing that contract. The sword quest, which looked like a MacGuffin, turns out to be the condition of the comeback. Bernstein blood was never just a bloodline quiz. It was the story insisting that the woman they tried to spend still holds the only key the throne cannot counterfeit. The ending is, by the standards of the shelf, shockingly willing to be an ending. Reviews from the years after still argue about whether the action in that last volume thins the filth, and that argument is itself proof of the work’s nerve. It would rather risk a climax than freeze the women in the profitable position. You are meant to leave with this. Survival is not a return to the woman you were. Survival is a refusal to give the room back. The bonus short that shipped with the box, a few minutes in late 2010, underlines the refusal in the crudest handwriting available. The pirates do not go home to innocence. They go home with the memory still installed, and with the people who arranged the memory now answering to the same grammar. Permanence is the punchline. Some transformations do not wash off, and the OVA is honest enough to treat that as the price of the win rather than a glitch to be patched.

What makes it stand out is the decision to be a serial with a spine. Episode one can pass for a story, which already embarrasses half the catalog. The twins of Gielen, the slave trade, the corrupt aristocrats, the silver knight crossing their route, all of that is scaffolding so the fall has a direction instead of a playlist. You do not need the play by play. You need the shape. A pirate knight hunts a sword. A proud knight hunts a tyrant. Both are caught by a house that has turned INTO cruelty into a business model. Both are spent. Both are rewritten. Both walk out holding the rewrite. Set that against the field and the field looks like furniture. Taimanin tapes, prison ship tapes, demon knight tapes, Pixy’s own neighbors on the shelf, often do one room perfectly and then reprint the room. Sara changes the room’s constitution. Sci fi is not set dressing. Distance from Earth means no village to run back to, no council, no convenient amnesia. The warlords are the weather. Supernatural inheritance is the only law that still bites. Futanari is not a category tag. It is the plot’s mutation. Even the censorship, the old pixel mosaic over the working parts, becomes part of the texture. Japan shipped this as a product that had to hide the exact inch it was selling, and the hiding makes the surrounding violence and the voice work do more of the labor. Kotone Hirokawa’s Sara and Nana Isaka’s Sylia carry scenes where the picture is  shy and the performance is not.

It became a small cultural icon for a precise tribe, not for the mainstream, and that is the correct size for the icon. On boards and review piles it sits in the stack people defend with embarrassing sincerity. One viewer calls it the masterpiece because Pixy put heart in it. Another calls it four episodes of torture and dares you to admit you stayed. Both are describing the same object. A score that hovers in the high sixes on a hentai index is not a failure here. Hentai scores are a joke, and a joke that still has thousands of logged viewers years later, plus a bonus that people hunt specifically, has done the only job a cult OVA can do. It became the reference point for a certain promise. If you want pirate frills, look elsewhere. If you want the version where the frills get torn off, the body is garrisoned, the garrison is answered, and the credits still roll on a woman who can lift the sword, this is the tape people name. The funny cultural fact is that its ending theme is called Rise for Pleasure, which is either the most honest title in the medium or a dare. You rose. The pleasure was not yours alone. The rise still counts.

The must watch claim is narrower than fan scripture and stronger for being narrow. It is not a must watch if you need tenderness, or clean consent, or women who remain the shape they started as. It is a must watch if you want to see the adult OVA format used at full pressure. Television hentai of the era, and most of what followed it, is a guest in someone else’s schedule. An OVA is a sealed room the studio paid for. Pixy, the house behind a run of hard tapes that later viewers file next to Taimanin Asagi, Kangoku Senkan, and Makai Kishi Ingrid, spent that room on a complete arc. Four volumes. A source novel from Lilith’s Black Lilith label, out in download and package form in August 2007. An adaptation that does not pretend the game and the animation are the same drawing. Design hands like Kuratch on the mechanical side, a harder anime line than the game’s softer faces, music under Michiguchi, direction associated with the EDEN credit, an ending song from the hime+ circle. None of that is trivia for its own sake. It is the reason the thing feels built. Someone storyboarded a fall and a reversal instead of padding a scene count. The game even hides a truer route behind nightly quizzes with Hans, a little mechanic so petty it becomes charming. Answer wrong and the man dies in a trap and the bad end opens. Answer in the right sequence and the women walk out with their companions intact. The animation throws that minigame away and still keeps the moral. Attention is the difference between a corpse and a crew.

So the takeaway, stripped of the costume, is this. Watch it for the argument, not the tour. A galaxy that prices women by reputation will eventually spend the reputation. A knight who believes the ballad will meet the ballad’s authors in a room with no music. A body can be used as a dock, a treasury, and a punishment, and the story that admits this without flinching is doing more honest political work than the polite shows that talk about empire and never show the invoice. The reversal matters because it does not launder the invoice. Sara and Sylia do not become untouched again. They become the ones holding the pen, the sword, and, in the mean little bonus, the schedule. That is the legend. Not that they were never opened. That the opening was not the last word, and that an OVA, of all the disposable shapes this medium uses, was willing to spend four volumes and a box set short to make the last word obscene, earned, and theirs.

STORY | CJI Surya Kant calls for balancing AI-driven judicial transformation with constitutional values

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has called for embracing digitalisation and artificial intelligence in the justice system while ensuring that technological advancement does not dilute the constitutional values of dignity, equality, liberty and fairness.

Addressing the opening session of the VII Congress of the Association of Asian Constitutional Courts (AACC) in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, the CJI said courts could not remain untouched by the rapid transformation brought about by technology.

"Technology is changing the way our societies function. It is changing the way governments deliver services, businesses operate and citizens interact with public institutions. Courts, too, cannot remain untouched by this transformation," he said.

Digitalisation offers enormous possibilities for the justice system, he said, adding that it can make courts more accessible, reduce delays and simplify procedures.

"Artificial intelligence can assist judges and court staff in research and in managing large volumes of information. These are opportunities that we must approach with openness and imagination.

"But technology also presents us with a more fundamental question: what must remain unchanged when everything around us is changing? For Constitutional Courts, the answer lies in the values we are entrusted to protect," he said.

The CJI said a court does not merely decide cases.

text:
Outrageous NFL Mock Trade:

Minnesota Vikings receive:
RB TreVeyon Henderson
OL Will Campbell
2027 1st-round pick
2028 1st-round pick
2028 3rd-round pick
2029 2nd-round pick

New England Patriots receive:
HC Kevin O’Connell 
WR Jordan Addison 
OG Will Fries

First of all, I do not think the Vikings do this, or even New England. This is just a fun hypothetical. There is historical precedent for 2 first round picks when trading younger head coaches. 

I believe the Wilfs would not trade KOC. Also, an important fact is Kevin O’Connell reports to ownership, not the GM, so Nolan Teasley cannot do this on his own.

Why do the Patriots do this?
New England is 1–2 after making the Super Bowl last year. The regression many saw coming has happened, and getting smoked by Jacksonville looked bad. Drake Maye has seemingly regressed, and the Patriots offense has been terrible going back to the start of last year’s playoffs.
There has also been a very public controversy involving Mike Vrabel and now former NFL insider Dianna Russini. The optics of what has been release has not been kind to Vrabel, but it is another source of noise around a team that already looks dysfunctional. It is well documented that Drake Maye is a religious person and when his coach is in this kind of controversy; it is possible a rift could develop. 

Now bring in former Patriots third-round pick Kevin O’Connell. Who is 46-25 as a coach. Among active HC's has a top 5 winning percentage. 
For a price, the Krafts can wipe their hands of Vrabel and bring in a former Coach of the Year who can help the Patriots’ biggest issues. 
If Kevin O’Connell has two strengths, they are culture building and calling plays for big-arm, mobile QBs. The Vikings were heavily linked to Drake Maye during the 2024 draft process, and Maye seemingly fits exactly what KOC wants physically at QB. KOC may not be a QB developer in the traditional sense, but he has shown he can build high level offenses with the right guy. Maye might be that guy. During the KOC era, there have been very few if any reports of locker room issues. His teams play hard and it appears there a great culture, unlike with his processor Mike Zimmer. 

Why do the Patriots make the player portion of the trade?

Will Campbell is not an NFL tackle, in my opinion. He was exposed in the playoffs, and New England drafting another tackle in the first round would be telling. They swap Campbell for Fries, who is not great but can stabilize the interior of their offensive line with someone in their natural position.  Losing Henderson hurts, but at the end of the day, teams can find RBs, while the new iteration of the Vikings clearly values the position more. The Patriots need another boost to their WR room, and Addison gives them someone who can step in and potentially be Maye’s guy for the next decade. When Jefferson has been out, Jordan has shown he can be WR1 for a great team. Plus, when A.J. Brown gets healthy, that offense could be special.

Finally, look at Detroit, 2 years ago it seemed their future was incredible. The now infamous quote from Dan Cambell "This may[e] have been our only chance." Drake Maye pun to prove his isn't AI. Anyway, building teams is very difficult, the Pats do a move to build around Drake Maye right now and keep him on the path to be an Elite QB with a coach that can maximize him. 

Why do the Vikings do this?

This is where it gets complicated.
Like I said, the Vikings love KOC. The Vikings have won 8 straight games dating back to last season. Mostly with bottom tier QB play. The brains of Brian Flores and the talent on that defense. Flores is once again regarded as one of the best defensive play callers in football. He is not going to be a DC forever. If the Vikings want to keep someone like that, eventually he needs a promotion. In this scenario, who calls the offense is a question. The solution, make a godfather offer to bring Grant Udinski back to Minnesota as OC. If the Wilfs do not want to promote Flores to HC, bring in Udinski as the head coach, make Flores assistant HC, and give him another raise. I think there is a way to make this work.

I also think it is notable that before Mike Tomlin became a head coach, he was the Vikings defensive coordinator and Minnesota let him walk out the door. More recently, I bet the Ravens wish they had kept Mike Macdonald. I bet Washington wishes it had found a way to keep Sean McVay. You cannot continually let great coordinators walk out the door.

As the Vikings shift their offensive philosophy toward running the football and winning with defense, do they really need two elite WRs? More importantly, can they pay both? No, they cannot.  Trade Addison for Henderson and add an elite, explosive talent at RB. Flip Fries for Will Campbell, who could eventually become the RG of the future of an elite young o-line. 

The future of the Vikings would be centered around an elite defense and a dominant running game, while adding a lot of draft capital.

In this hypothetical trade…

Who says no?
